risks.note: MD&A Risks and Concerns: profitability and cost effectiveness may be affected by a rise in the prices of raw materials and other inputs. The Outlook adds that the sector is grappling with fluctuating prices of steel, aluminium, copper and precious metals plus increasing fuel prices, making the year likely to be a challenging one for the auto component industry.

The business is characterised by a limited customer base coupled with intense competition from suppliers operating in both the organised and unorganised sectors. Management separately flags that increasing competition in the auto equipment sector may put pressure on market share.

The Company deals principally in only one segment - automotive components - so segment-wise performance is not applicable, leaving earnings fully exposed to the Indian automotive cycle. (The BRSR figure of 96.56% of turnover from automotive components under NIC code 2811 sits in the profile/registry bundles of this same annual report, not in this one.)

MD&A Risks and Concerns: the automobile industry is a technical intensive industry facing constant demand for new designs and knowledge of nascent technology. The regulatory shift to CAFE III norms, Stage V emission standards, alternate fuels, rising EV penetration, enhanced safety regulations and vehicle scrappage is driving a fundamental change in vehicle technologies and product architecture, with success dependent on technological leadership, specialisation and innovation capability.
risks.risk: Technology transition and technical intensity of the industry

risks.note: MD&A Risks and Concerns names foreign currency risk explicitly: exchange rate fluctuations may have an adverse impact on the Company. (The BRSR disclosure of exports at 8.4% of total turnover and markets served across 19 international countries sits in the profile/registry bundles of this same annual report, not in this one.)

MD&A Risks and Concerns: ongoing geopolitical tensions, particularly the conflict in West Asia including the Israel-Hamas war, have contributed to increases in crude oil and other commodity prices, exerting upward pressure on inflation. The Outlook adds global trade and tariff uncertainties and risks around transmission of West Asia developments to fuel prices, supply chains and consumer sentiment.

Outlook: supply chain stability, particularly for critical components, remains an area of ongoing concern; the industry navigated semiconductor chip shortages and other supply chain constraints during FY 2025-26.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
